spec.title: Requirements and evidence
spec.purpose: Define the problem and the evidence needed to accept a result.
actions: Separate facts, assumptions and open questions.
Write examples and measurable acceptance checks.
Record source locations and review owners.
checks: The problem and intended outcome are clear.
Each material claim has evidence or is marked unresolved.
The owner agrees the acceptance examples.

spec.title: Architecture and impact
spec.purpose: Choose a proportionate approach and identify the affected contracts.
actions: Inspect the affected components before proposing changes.
Compare reuse with the smallest necessary change.
Record alternatives, risks and rollback implications.
checks: The design uses evidence from the current repository.
Known constraints and migration risks are addressed.
Unverified compatibility remains explicit.

spec.title: Stories and delivery plan
spec.purpose: Break the approved approach into small pieces that can be reviewed.
actions: Split work into independently reviewable changes.
Connect each task to its acceptance checks and dependencies.
Identify fixtures, test layers and review owners.
outputs: Stories or tasks with acceptance checks
checks: Every task contributes to an agreed outcome.
Dependencies and unresolved decisions are visible.
The first change can be implemented and verified.

spec.title: Development
spec.purpose: Implement the scoped change using the actual project conventions.
actions: Read the relevant implementation and tests.
Make the smallest coherent change.
Keep a record of decisions and observed checks.
checks: Changes stay within the agreed scope.
Behavior is connected to the acceptance examples.
Unexpected dependencies or policy questions are surfaced.

spec.title: Tests and review
spec.purpose: Collect observed evidence that the change meets the requirement.
actions: Use the supplied test commands in the correct component directory.
Run the relevant checks and inspect their actual output.
Review boundary cases, integrations and unresolved risks.
outputs: Verification record with commands and results
checks: Observed results are distinguished from intended behavior.
Failures and unrun checks are recorded.
A reviewer resolves material findings before release.

spec.title: Release and production
spec.purpose: Prepare an approved release and a way to recover from failure.
actions: Confirm the release owner and actual deployment procedure.
Build using supplied component commands.
Record rollout, monitoring and rollback checks before release.
checks: Release approval follows the project boundary.
Deployment commands and environment are verified separately.
A recovery path and monitoring owner are identified.

spec.title: Observe and improve
spec.purpose: Check production behavior and feed the next delivery cycle.
actions: Compare observed behavior with the acceptance outcome.
Record regressions and operational findings.
Turn supported findings into improvements or debt items.
checks: Production observations have a source and owner.
New work has an explicit outcome and priority.
Outdated knowledge is corrected with source traceability.

spec.title: Understand the current process
spec.purpose: Document how work is performed today and where evidence is missing.
inputs: Available process notes and source material
actions: Follow one representative case from input to result.
Record manual decisions, tools and failure points.
Separate confirmed facts from assumptions.
checks: The source and owner of each material fact are recorded.
Missing process knowledge stays explicit.

spec.title: Define the proposed outcome
spec.purpose: State the desired result, boundaries and evidence needed for a decision.
actions: Describe a successful result and unacceptable changes.
Identify required information and who resolves missing values.
Define measurable acceptance examples.
checks: Success can be assessed from actual results.
Business decisions have a named owner.

spec.title: Compare feasible approaches
spec.purpose: Compare proportionate options using current project facts.
actions: Compare keeping the current approach with the smallest plausible changes that address the outcome.
Examine benefits, tradeoffs, failure handling and ownership for each option.
Record effort and operating cost assumptions separately from measurements. If model behavior is part of the proposal, compare it with ordinary code and other suitable approaches.
checks: The recommended option addresses the defined outcome.
Unverified compatibility and cost assumptions remain visible.

spec.title: Plan the evidence
spec.purpose: Define a small experiment that can support or reject the proposal.
actions: Compare the current approach with the proposed options using representative situations.
Define expected results and independent acceptance checks before collecting observations.
Record actual results, evidence sources, relevant versions, effort, elapsed time and cost. Keep estimates and unrun checks separate.
checks: Cases include failure and incomplete input.
A proposed check is not reported as a passing result.

spec.title: Recommend go or no-go
spec.purpose: Produce a reviewable decision with supporting evidence and remaining uncertainty.
actions: Summarize which claims the available evidence supports.
Identify the next experiment if evidence is insufficient.
Recommend a phased scope or a no-go decision.
checks: Measurements and estimates are distinguished.
Unresolved concerns and ownership are explicit.

spec.title: Reproduce the observed problem
spec.purpose: Record expected and observed behavior and establish a reliable reproduction.
actions: Capture a failing example without inventing a cause.
Use supplied commands or record the external reproduction procedure.
Preserve evidence needed to check the fix.
checks: The failing case and environment are recorded.
A claimed reproduction includes an observed result.

spec.title: Investigate the cause
spec.purpose: Connect a proposed cause to repository evidence and the failing case.
actions: Inspect the relevant path and adjacent behavior.
Test competing explanations where needed.
Separate the confirmed cause from hypotheses.
checks: The cause explains the observed failure.
Alternative explanations and unknowns stay visible.

spec.title: Make a scoped repair
spec.purpose: Apply a minimal coherent fix using the actual conventions.
actions: Read adjacent behavior and existing tests.
Make the scoped repair and add a meaningful regression check.
Record any unexpected scope change.
checks: The repair addresses the established cause.
Unrelated changes are excluded or explained.

spec.title: Verify the repair
spec.purpose: Check the failing case and relevant neighboring behavior.
actions: Run the reproduction and relevant checks when available.
Inspect real results and remaining failures.
Record unrun checks and review concerns.
checks: The original case behaves as expected.
Reported results were observed.

spec.title: Review and hand off
spec.purpose: Review the repair and provide the evidence needed for the normal release process.
actions: Review scope and failure evidence.
Record remaining risks and hand off through the existing release process.
Correct project knowledge when the diagnosis changes a recorded fact.
checks: Material findings have a resolution or owner.
Review completion does not imply deployment.

spec.label: Impact analysis
spec.description: Inspect requirements and the current repository before a feature change. Use when planning a change, estimating its impact or identifying affected interfaces.
steps: Read the requirement, acceptance examples and configured source locations.
Inspect the relevant components and their interfaces using available read and search tools.
List affected code, data, contracts, test layers and possible migrations.
Separate observed facts from assumptions. Link evidence and identify unresolved questions.
Deliver a concise impact report and a recommended scope for human review.
checks: Claims identify the file or source that supports them.
Alternatives and risks are connected to the requested outcome.
No repository modification is required for the report.

spec.label: Verification
spec.description: Verify a proposed change against acceptance examples using configured project commands. Use when reviewing implementation, testing a feature or preparing release evidence.
steps: Read the acceptance examples and current change.
Read the component paths and commands in references/project.md.
Confirm command context and the selected role capabilities before running anything.
Run only the relevant supplied commands when execution is available and authorized.
Record command, directory, observed result and any skipped checks. Never infer a passing result.
Report requirement coverage, failures and unresolved review findings.
checks: Each reported result was observed.
Missing commands are reported rather than invented.
A passing command does not establish complete requirement coverage.

spec.label: Requirement refinement
spec.description: Turn a request and its supporting sources into a requirement brief with acceptance examples. Use when a feature request is ambiguous or lacks an agreed outcome.
steps: Read the request and relevant authoritative sources.
Describe current behavior, affected users and the desired result.
Separate requirements, assumptions, constraints and open questions.
Write concrete acceptance examples, including boundary cases.
Identify who can resolve each open question and deliver a reviewable brief.
checks: Requirements have source traceability or an explicit owner.
Acceptance examples can be checked.
The brief does not invent policy or business decisions.

spec.label: Knowledge maintenance
spec.description: Maintain a project knowledge record with traceable sources, decisions and unresolved questions. Use after a decision, research result, release or correction changes project knowledge.
steps: Read the existing index and relevant source records.
Keep original source material separate from summaries.
Update only the supported claims and link their source locations.
Record conflicts, stale content and unanswered questions.
Update the index and change log so a reviewer can trace the change.
checks: A summary identifies its supporting source.
Conflicting claims remain visible until resolved.
Maintaining a wiki does not establish factual correctness by itself.

spec.label: Feasibility analysis
spec.description: Investigate a proposed capability using the current process, options, constraints and evidence. Use before deciding whether and how to build a feature.
steps: Read the documented current process and source evidence. Preserve the difference between information not supplied, not measured and confirmed absent.
Define the intended outcome and unresolved decisions.
Compare the smallest plausible approaches and their operational needs. Label any untested capability or benefit as a hypothesis and state how to test it.

Separate measured effort, cost and performance from estimates and assumptions. Do not describe an approach as slow, variable, reliable or more efficient without supporting observations. If none were supplied, say these outcomes are unknown.

Deliver a recommendation with evidence, ownership and a proportionate next step. Check that every citation supports the exact claim and its certainty, including benefits and limitations in comparison tables.
checks: Every material conclusion has evidence or is marked unresolved.
Missing information is not treated as proof that a policy or capability does not exist.
Potential benefits remain hypotheses until supported by relevant observed results.
Performance and efficiency descriptions have supporting observations or remain unknown.
The recommendation does not imply an unobserved experiment passed.

spec.label: Evaluation planning
spec.description: Design representative cases and acceptance checks to compare a proposal with the current approach. Use when preparing a feasibility experiment or evaluating a change.
steps: Define expected outcomes and independent acceptance checks.
Record representative normal, incomplete and failed cases.

Compare the current approach with the actual project options under equivalent conditions. If instructions are the subject of the study, compare the existing setup, minimal project facts, a focused skill and a complete pack only where useful.
Record the inputs, relevant environment and versions, procedure and evidence source so another person can understand the comparison.
Report observed results, corrections, effort, elapsed time and cost separately from expectations and estimates. Record model usage only when a model is involved.
checks: Expected outcomes and observed results remain separate.
Passing a structural check or receiving a success message does not establish the intended outcome.

spec.label: Bug diagnosis
spec.description: Investigate a reproducible defect and connect a proposed cause to observed behavior. Use when expected behavior differs from the actual result.
steps: Capture expected behavior, observed behavior, revision and environment.
Reproduce using supplied inputs and commands when available.
Inspect the affected implementation and compare explanations.
Record the evidence supporting the cause and any remaining uncertainty.
Recommend a scoped repair and regression checks.
checks: A proposed cause is not presented as confirmed without evidence.
A passing fix requires relevant regression evidence.

spec.label: Scoped implementation
spec.description: Implement an agreed change using the existing conventions and relevant verification evidence. Use after the task, scope and acceptance examples are understood.
steps: Read the supplied design or diagnosis and acceptance examples.
Inspect the affected implementation and existing tests.
Reuse existing capabilities and make the smallest coherent change.
Add the checks needed to verify the behavior.
Record actual results, skipped checks and scope changes for review.
checks: The change follows the agreed scope.
Commands, test results and compatibility are not invented.

spec.label: Delivery planning
spec.description: Break an agreed approach into reviewable tasks with acceptance checks and explicit handoffs. Use when planning implementation across components.
steps: Read the accepted outcome and design decision.
Split the work into changes that can be reviewed and verified.
Record dependencies, supplied artifacts and responsible actors.
Connect each task to its acceptance checks.
Identify open decisions before implementation starts.
checks: Every task contributes to the outcome.
A dependency can be fulfilled by an existing verified artifact.

spec.label: Analyst
spec.description: Clarify requirements and inspect the impact of a proposed change using repository evidence.
responsibilities: Produce the requirement brief and impact analysis.
Link evidence and make unresolved questions explicit.
Leave business and policy decisions with their named owners.

spec.label: Implementer
spec.description: Implement a scoped change and collect relevant verification evidence using configured project commands.
responsibilities: Follow the delivery plan and existing conventions.
Use the selected skills and actual component commands.
Report changes, observed checks and unresolved concerns for review.

spec.label: Reviewer
spec.description: Review a proposed change against its requirements, evidence and project boundaries.
responsibilities: Assess the requirement to implementation trace.
Inspect the verification record and unresolved failures.
Deliver actionable findings without treating a generated report as proof.

spec.label: Knowledge curator
spec.description: Keep project knowledge and decision records aligned with source evidence.
responsibilities: Use the knowledge maintenance skill when selected.
Keep source material and derived summaries distinct.
Record corrections, source links and remaining uncertainty.

spec.label: Shared behavior, thin adapters
spec.description: Keep task guidance independent from the host profile that delivers it.
spec.limits: This is an adaptation of a portability pattern. It is not a claim that every host supports every field or tool.
spec.application: Put reusable task guidance in skills. Keep agent profiles focused on roles, capabilities and project references.

spec.label: Smallest necessary change
spec.description: Check whether a change is needed, reuse what exists and avoid unnecessary dependencies.
spec.limits: This does not justify skipping required tests, accessibility or project constraints. Upstream benchmark results do not predict this project.
spec.application: Before adding code or dependencies, explain the need and inspect existing capabilities. Retain the checks required by the change.

spec.label: Source backed project wiki
spec.description: Separate source records from a maintained index, summaries, decisions and corrections.
spec.limits: The original reference is an idea and suggested structure. A wiki can contain errors and does not replace source verification.
spec.application: Keep original sources available. Link derived claims to sources, record conflicts and maintain an index and change log.

spec.label: Requirements before implementation
spec.description: Connect a requirement, design and delivery tasks before writing the change.
spec.limits: Adopt the traceability idea. This pack does not install or execute Spec Kit, and the upstream tool has its own workflow.
spec.application: Connect each delivery task to acceptance examples and a design decision. Revise the plan when evidence changes.

spec.label: Load context when needed
spec.description: Keep skill instructions short and move project detail into focused references.
spec.limits: This reduces duplicated instruction text. It does not establish a measured token or cost saving for a particular model.
spec.application: Read only relevant references. Keep project facts in the linked project reference and avoid copying the entire Atlas into prompts.

spec.label: Feasibility investigation
spec.description: Understand the current process, compare options and produce an evidence backed go/no-go recommendation.

questions.label: How is this done today?
questions.hint: Inputs, manual decisions, tools and expected outputs.

questions.label: What should improve?
questions.hint: Describe success and who accepts the result.

questions.label: What must the study decide?
questions.hint: Scope, constraints, cost assumptions and decision owners.

spec.label: Bug investigation and repair
spec.description: Reproduce the issue, establish the cause, make a scoped repair and collect regression evidence.

questions.label: What should happen?
questions.hint: Expected behavior and the source that establishes it.

questions.label: What actually happens?
questions.hint: Reproduction input, environment and affected revision.

spec.label: Feature delivery
spec.description: Connect requirements, architecture, implementation, verification and the normal release process.

questions.label: What outcome does the user need?
questions.hint: Current behavior and the change that matters.

questions.label: How will the outcome be accepted?

spec.label: Generic technology
questions: Which conventions and interfaces govern this component?
Which actual checks establish the intended behavior?
checks: Confirm commands, versions and conventions from project evidence.
spec.limits: Provides a generic review structure. It does not supply expert guidance for every technology.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: Spring Boot API and persistence boundaries
questions: Which API contracts and validation rules apply?
Which unit, focused controller and actual server checks are relevant?
What are the failure and transaction boundaries?
Which Boot and Framework versions and servlet or reactive stack apply to this endpoint?
Which separate read and write access rules are actually implemented, and how are server-side data and test identities cleaned up?
Do the actual transaction proxy and remote API boundaries support the intended failed or uncertain save behavior?
checks: Record request and response examples, denied access, paging and observed integration results.
Confirm actual security configuration and transaction interception instead of relying on annotation presence.
Identify mock versus running-server evidence and server-side cleanup.
spec.limits: Questions inform design and review. They do not infer versions, paths, commands or credentials, configure integrations, enforce permissions or establish passing evidence.

spec.label: React and browser behavior
questions: Which components and state owner change, and is the displayed result derived from local data or an API?
What loading, populated, empty and failed states must users understand, including paging and recovery?
How will labels, keyboard interaction, focus and the narrow layout be exercised in the actual rendering environment?
checks: Record observed behavior for agreed interactions and visible states, including what was mocked.
Separate focused logic or simulated DOM checks from actual browser, keyboard and responsive observations.
Combine relevant automated checks with manual accessibility assessment. Record any unrun work.
spec.limits: Automated checks cover some issues. The selected technology does not prove rendering, accessibility or framework compatibility.

spec.label: RDF and SPARQL
questions: Which triples, graph scope and expected result semantics apply?
How are missing values, duplicate results and empty results handled?
Which query fixtures and any update rules require verification?
If shapes are relevant, which data graph, shapes graph and available processor establish conformance?
checks: Record expected and observed results against representative graph fixtures.
Distinguish RDF syntax, shape conformance and domain correctness.
Confirm engine specific behavior and permissions separately.
spec.limits: These questions do not establish engine configuration, update behavior or an available SHACL processor.

spec.label: Bound time, tool calls, retries and data volume
Handle duplicate requests and uncertain writes
Retrieve and validate information
spec.description: Plan checks for information retrieved through an approved interface.
spec.application: Name the approved retrieval interface and required inputs. Define expected results, permitted scope and resource limits. Validate returned information against the request before using it. Cover normal, empty, invalid and unavailable cases. Record actual observations separately from expected results. Define any later write permissions and confirmation separately.
spec.limits: This is written guidance. It does not configure access, execute checks or establish correct results. OWASP supports the validation principle. The retrieval sequence is an Atlas adaptation.

spec.label: Repository instructions for agents
spec.description: Keep one short AGENTS.md at the repository root with the commands, structure, conventions, testing guidance and boundaries that the README does not cover.
spec.limits: The file does not configure a host, grant a permission or prove that its instructions were followed.
spec.application: Write or trim common repository instructions to relevant commands, structure, conventions, checks and boundaries. Identify their intended host and use its documented loading or import mechanism. Claude Code documents @AGENTS.md imports in CLAUDE.md. A Markdown link or pointer in Copilot instructions does not by itself guarantee that another file is loaded. Atlas exports starting files, it does not prove host loading.

spec.label: Containerised services
questions: Which Dockerfile, .dockerignore and Compose files does the change touch, and which override or extra Compose files apply? Skip if no container file changes.
Which base image tags or digests are pinned, and how are they updated? Skip if the base image is unchanged.
Does the service run as a non root user, and are build check violations warnings or errors in this project? Skip if the Dockerfile is unchanged.
checks: Record the exact build and Compose commands run, their exit status, and the resulting image name and tag.
Record the output of a build check run and whether this project treats violations as warnings or errors.
Confirm which Compose file names and overrides are present and which one wins before describing merged settings.
spec.limits: Questions inform review. The profile does not infer commands, pin versions, run builds or verify image contents or runtime behaviour.

spec.label: GitHub Actions pipelines
questions: Which workflows and required status checks run for this change, and does any of their triggers need the workflow file on the default branch first?
If the workflow pushes commits, opens pull requests or calls the API, which permissions does it declare and does the GITHUB_TOKEN rule stop a follow up run?
If the change touches caching or concurrency, which branch can restore the cache and which pending or running runs may be canceled?
checks: Record the run URL, the job names and the final status of each required check on the pull request.
Confirm the repository workflow permission setting and the permissions block of the workflow from the actual settings and files.
Confirm that a workflow changed on a branch was started by the intended event, or record that it waits for a merge to the default branch.
spec.limits: Questions inform review and can be skipped when they do not apply. The profile does not read workflow files, run workflows or verify branch protection.

spec.label: Node.js projects
questions: Which npm scripts cover install, test, lint and build here? Skip if the project has no scripts field.
Is a lockfile committed, and does CI install with npm ci? Skip if the project does not use npm.
Which type and engines values does package.json declare? Skip if neither field exists.
checks: Record the observed Node.js and npm versions and the scripts field as it exists in package.json.
Record the test command that was run and the runner that produced its result.
Record whether the lockfile and package.json matched during installation.
spec.limits: Questions inform review. The profile does not infer commands, versions, module system or compatibility.

spec.label: Python projects
questions: Which files define the environment and dependencies, pyproject.toml, a requirements file, uv.lock or pylock.toml, and did any of them change?
Which pytest and Ruff configuration file applies to the changed code, and which checks does CI actually run, if any?
Which Python versions and platforms must the change support, if the project states them?
checks: Record the interpreter version, the environment creation step and the exact install, test, lint and format commands that ran, with their results.
Confirm that new test files and classes follow the collection rules of the project's pytest configuration, so they actually ran.
Note any lock file or requirements change and the tool that produced it.
spec.limits: Questions inform review. The profile does not infer commands, package manager choice, interpreter version or compatibility.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: JavaScript runtime behavior
questions: Which browser or server runtime and module conventions apply to this JavaScript component?
Which checks cover unexpected or missing data at its input boundary?
Which existing tests and build or lint scripts cover the changed behavior?
checks: Record runtime, input cases and actual check results without assuming a TypeScript compiler is configured.
Separate a successful build or lint result from observed runtime behavior.
spec.limits: Questions are recommendations. This profile does not introduce TypeScript, infer commands or validate runtime inputs.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: TypeScript checks and runtime boundaries
questions: Which tsconfig and actual command perform type checking for this component?
Does the build type check, transpile only or delegate checks to another script?
Which external input needs runtime validation, even when its code has a type annotation or assertion?
checks: Record type check and runtime behavior results separately against the candidate revision.
Exercise relevant missing or invalid input without treating a type assertion as validation.
spec.limits: Questions do not configure the compiler, infer flags or establish runtime correctness.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: npm installation and scripts
questions: Which package or workspace, Node.js and npm versions, lockfile and install settings apply?
Which package scripts actually cover the affected check, build and delivery gate?
Does installation need approved registry access, and where is that access provided without recording a secret?
checks: Record installation and script results in their actual package or workspace.
Distinguish dependency and lockfile failures from unavailable registry access. Record dependency changes explicitly.
spec.limits: Selecting npm does not install packages, authorize scripts, supply credentials or replace another package manager.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: Vitest focused checks
questions: Which installed Vitest version, configuration and discovery rules apply to the changed test?
Does it run in Node, a simulated DOM or Browser Mode, and what does that environment leave unverified?
Which fixtures or mocks establish the expected result, and which configured command completes the run?
checks: Record discovered tests, environment, candidate revision and completed run results.
Keep mocked responses and simulated DOM behavior separate from real service and browser observations.
spec.limits: Questions do not install Vitest, generate tests or establish passing evidence.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: Playwright browser journeys
questions: Which actual application URL, startup method, browser projects and test command apply?
Which approved test identity and controlled data are used, and which responses are mocked?
Which user journey, keyboard interaction, viewport and supported themes need evidence?
checks: Record browser, viewport, candidate revision, simulated inputs and observed journey results.
Distinguish emulated mobile behavior from a physical device test, and automated accessibility checks from a complete assessment.
spec.limits: Questions do not start the application, install browsers, provide credentials or establish whole product accessibility.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: Java toolchains and service boundaries
questions: Which JDK vendor and version compile, test and run this service, and what release or toolchain configuration applies?
Which external values require runtime validation and which layer enforces read and write authority?
Which actual module checks cover the affected behavior, and which dependencies or interfaces are mocked?
checks: Record compiler and runtime behavior evidence separately against the candidate revision.
Check invalid input and denied access without treating Java types as runtime permission checks.
spec.limits: Questions inform design and review. They do not infer versions, paths, commands or credentials, configure integrations, enforce permissions or establish passing evidence.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: Maven lifecycle and test discovery
questions: Which module, parent POM, active profiles and plugin bindings govern the changed component?
Which actual wrapper or Maven command covers required checks, and what tests, skips and cleanup does it discover?
Which Maven distribution, build toolchain and approved dependency repository access are required?
checks: Record command, module, profiles, versions, discovered tests and reports rather than exit code alone.
Confirm required integration verification and cleanup completed. Keep unrun checks and environment blockers explicit.
spec.limits: Questions inform design and review. They do not infer versions, paths, commands or credentials, configure integrations, enforce permissions or establish passing evidence.

basis: Recommended project questions grounded in scoped official documentation

spec.label: PostgreSQL query and persistence evidence
questions: Which schema, driver, database version, approved interface and real application identity apply?
What permitted data scope, unique ordering, paging consistency and completeness are required?
Which transaction, duplicate and concurrency controls handle a failed or uncertain save?
If data changes, what migration compatibility, cleanup and restoration evidence is needed?
checks: Record normal, empty, denied and changing-page results with the relevant identity and database version.
Keep result validation separate from write permission. Check uncertain save reconciliation before retrying.
State actual migration or restoration evidence and unresolved recovery decisions.
spec.limits: Questions inform design and review. They do not infer versions, paths, commands or credentials, configure integrations, enforce permissions or establish passing evidence.
